rubric:
1. Says the kernel is latency-bound: neither memory nor compute is near its peak.
2. Connects the low occupancy to the 255 registers per thread (registers allow only 8 warps, one block, per SM) and notes too few warps are in flight to hide memory latency.
3. Proposes reducing register use (e.g. `__launch_bounds__`, less unrolling) or smaller blocks so more warps are resident.
4. Proposes more memory parallelism per thread: vectorized loads (e.g. 16-byte loads of 8 BF16), several rows per block or multiple loads in flight.
5. Says how to confirm the fix: DRAM throughput should rise toward peak, since LayerNorm is memory-bound at its best.
